title: Downloaded Video Won't Play? Causes and How to Fix It
description: Downloaded video won't play? Find out why, from an unfinished download to the HEVC codec, and follow these practical fixes to get it playing again.
photoCaption: An unsupported format can stop a video from playing.
photo2Caption: Try another video option or another player.
body:
The video downloaded fine, but when you open it you get an error message, a black screen or choppy playback? Don't give up just yet. There are a few common reasons why a downloaded video won't play, and most of them you can fix yourself in a few minutes. Let's go through them one by one.

For reference, MP4 files downloaded from I Need Save already have the correct duration and play in gallery apps. So if something's wrong, the cause is usually one of the following.

1. The download isn't finished

Some videos need to be processed before downloading, for example by joining the video and audio, or converting a stream into MP4. While this is happening, the button shows Preparing…. If you close the page or lose your connection before the download finishes, the file can end up corrupted or incomplete.

Fix: download the video again, wait for the download to start automatically, and make sure it has finished in your browser's downloads list before you open the file.

2. The video codec isn't supported on an old phone

Some TikTok videos use the HEVC (H.265) codec. It makes files more efficient, but very old phones may not be able to play it smoothly. Symptoms include choppy playback, a black screen with only sound, or the gallery app refusing to open the file.

Fix: download again and choose another available video option. H.264 options play on almost every device. You can also choose a lower resolution to make it lighter. Also read the difference between 360p, 720p and 1080p video quality to help you choose.

3. The video hasn't shown up in the Gallery yet

On Android, files are saved in the Downloads folder, and the Gallery app sometimes takes a moment to show them. You might think the video is broken when it simply hasn't been picked up yet.

Fix: open the file directly from your file manager or from the browser's downloads list. Or wait a little, then reopen the Gallery app.

4. On iPhone, the video is still in the Files app

iPhone and iPad users on Safari often get confused because the video isn't in the Photos app. That's because downloaded files go to the Files app → Downloads.

  1. Open the Files app and go to the Downloads folder.
  2. Tap the video you just downloaded.
  3. Tap Share.
  4. Choose Save Video.

After that, you can play the video from the Photos app. There's a full guide to file locations in our article on where downloaded files are saved.

5. What you downloaded isn't actually a video

Besides video, the list of options also includes Audio and Photo / Thumbnail. If you picked audio by accident, you saved a sound file with no picture. If you picked the thumbnail, all you saved was the cover image.

Fix: repeat the process and make sure you tap a video option in the quality you want.

6. Storage is full or the player app is acting up

Nearly full storage can cause files to be saved incompletely. An outdated player app or operating system can also have trouble opening certain videos.

Fix: free up some storage, install any available updates for your system and gallery app, then download the video again.

A quick fix that often helps: delete the problem file, copy the link again from the Share button, then download it again with a different quality option.

How to download again the right way

  1. In the social media app, tap Share and then Copy link.
  2. Open the I Need Save downloader page.
  3. Paste the link or tap Paste, then press Download.
  4. Choose the right video option, and wait if you see Preparing….

Keep in mind that private content, content that requires a login and region-restricted content can't be downloaded. Only save videos for personal use, and if you want to repost, ask the creator for permission and give credit.

Frequently asked questions

Why is there sound but a black picture?

Usually because the phone doesn't support that video codec, such as HEVC on a very old device. Try downloading again with another video option.

Can a downloaded video have the wrong duration?

MP4 files from I Need Save already have the correct duration. If the duration looks odd, the download probably didn't finish, so try downloading again.

The video plays on my laptop but not on my phone. Why?

Most likely because the two devices support different codecs. Try choosing another video option when downloading for your phone.
